## tal-a23-p04 (23.31-23.40)
[and]-prāptābhiṣekaḥ sa guruḥ ṣaṇmāsānmantrapaddhatim / sarvāṃ tantroditāṃ dhyāyejjapeccātanmayatvataḥ yadaiva tanmayībhūtastadā vīryamupāgataḥ / chindyātpāśāṃstato yatnaṃ kuryāttanmayatāsthitau hṛccakrādutthitā sūkṣmā śaśisphaṭikasaṃnibhā / lekhākārā nādarūpā praśāntā cakrapaṅktigā dvādaśānte nirūḍhā sā sauṣumne tripathāntare / tatra hṛccakramāpūrya japenmantraṃ jvalatprabham cakṣurlomādirandhraughavahajjvālaurvasaṃnibham / yāvacchāntaśikhākīrṇaṃ viśvājyapravilāpakam tadājyadhārāsaṃtṛptamānābhikuharāntaram / evaṃ mantrā mokṣadāḥ syurdīptā buddhāḥ sunirmalāḥ mūlakandanabhonābhihṛtkaṇṭhālikatālugam / ardhendurodhikānādatadantavyāpiśaktigam samanonmanaśuddhātmaparacakrasamāśritam / yatra yatra japeccakre samastavyastabhedanāt tatra tatra mahāmantra iti devyākhyayāmale / vidyāvratamidaṃ proktaṃ mantravīryaprasiddhaye tacca tādātmyameveti yaduktaṃ spandaśāsane / tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ sarvajñabalaśālinaḥ

## tal-a23-p05 (23.41-23.50)
[and]-pravartante@dhikārāya karaṇānīva dehinām / kṛtavidyāvrataḥ paścāddīkṣāvyākhyādi sarvataḥ kuryādyogyeṣu śiṣyeṣu nāyogyeṣu kadācana / rahasye yojayedvipraṃ parīkṣya viparītataḥ ācārācchaktimapyeva nānyathetyūrmiśāsane / nityādyalpālpakaṃ kuryādyaduktaṃ brahmayāmale cīrṇavidyāvrataḥ sarvaṃ manasā vā smaretpriye / dehasaṃbandhasaṃchannasārvajñyo dambhabhājanam avidandīkṣamāṇo@pi na duṣyeddaiśikaḥ kvacit / jñātvā tvayogyatāṃ nainaṃ dīkṣeta pratyavāyitām buddhvā jñāne śāstrasiddhigurutvādau ca taṃ punaḥ / bhūya eva parīkṣeta tattadaucityaśālinam tatra tatra niyuñjīta natu jātu viparyayāt / nanu tadvastvayogyasya tatrecchā jāyate kutaḥ tadīśādhiṣṭhitecchaiva yogyatāmasya sūcayet / satyaṃ kāpi prabuddhāsāvicchā rūḍhiṃ na gacchati vidyudvatpāpaśīlasya yathā pāpāpavarjane / rūḍhyarūḍhī tadicchāyā api śaṃbhuprasādataḥ aprarūḍhatathecchākastata eva na bhājanam / yaḥ samyagjñānamādāya guruviśvāsavarjitaḥ

## tal-a23-p06 (23.51-23.60)

## tal-a23-p07 (23.61-23.70)
[and]-śivābhedena tatkuryāttadvatpañcamamapyayam / tirobhāvābhidhaṃ kṛtyaṃ tathāsau śivatātmakaḥ ata eva śive śāstre jñāne cāśvāsabhājanam / gurormūḍhatayā kopadhāmāpi na tirohitaḥ gururhi kupito yasya sa tirohita ucyate / saṃsārī satu devo hi gururna ca mṛṣāvidaḥ tata eva ca śāstrādidūṣako yadyapi krudhā / na dahyate@sau guruṇā tathāpyeṣa tirohitaḥ asmadgurvāgamastveṣa tirobhūte svayaṃ śiśau / na kupyenna śapeddhīmān sa hyanugrāhakaḥ sadā īśecchācoditaḥ pāśaṃ yadi kaṇṭhe nipīḍayet / kimācāryeṇa tatrāsya kāryā syātsahakāritā śivābhinno@pi hi gururanugrahamayīṃ vibhoḥ / mukhyāṃ śaktimupāsīno@nugṛhṇīyātsa sarvathā svātantryamātrajñaptyai tu kathitaṃ śāstra īdṛśam / na kāryaṃ patatāṃ hastālambaḥ sahyo na pātanam ata eva svatantratvādicchāyāḥ punarunmukham / prāyaścittairviśodhyainaṃ dīkṣeta kṛpayā guruḥ ūrdhvadṛṣṭau prapannaḥ sannanāśvastastataḥ param / adhaḥśāstraṃ prapadyāpi na śreyaḥpātratāmiyāt

## tal-a23-p08 (23.71-23.80)
[and]-adhodṛṣṭau prapannastu tadanāśvastamānasaḥ / ūrdhvaśāsanabhāk pāpaṃ taccojjhecca śivībhavet rājñe druhyannamātyāṅgabhūto@pi hi vihanyate / viparyayastu netyevamūrdhvāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ samāśrayet śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ yāvattenaiva noddhṛtaḥ / atra hyartho@yametāvatpūrvoktajñānavṛṃhitaḥ gurustāvatsa evātra tacchabdenāvamṛśyate / tādṛksvabhyastavijñānabhājordhvapadaśālinā anuddhṛtasya na śreya etadanyagurūddhṛteḥ / ata evāmbujanmārkadṛṣṭānto@tra nirūpitaḥ trijagajjyotiṣo hyanyattejo@nyacca niśākṛtaḥ / jñānamanyattrikaguroranyattvadharavartinām ata eva purābhūtagurvabhāvo yadā tadā / tadanyaṃ lakṣaṇopetamāśrayetpunarunmukhaḥ sati tasmiṃstūnmukhaḥ sankasmājjahyādyadi sphuṭam / syādanyatarago doṣo yo@dhikārāpaghātakaḥ doṣaśceha na lokastho doṣatvena nirūpyate / ajñānakhyāpanāyuktakhyāpanātmā tvasau mataḥ śiṣyasyāpi tathābhūtajñānānāśvastarūpatā / mukhyo doṣastadanye hi doṣāstatprabhavā yataḥ

args.topic: Tantraloka 23 abhisekaprakasana: consecration of a teacher
args.excerpts:
[Dupuche, The Kula Ritual, ch.29 + consecration]
Ordinary initiation (samaya-dīkṣā) is essentially a prelude. In TĀ 29 the term dīkṣā properly speaking is reserved to initiation as a Son (putraka), of which there are four types: sabīja (with set ritual and way of life) or nirbīja (without); if he seeks liberation he is called niṣkala.
The initiation described in the Ratnamālā involves the mantra KṢRAUṂ and 'oblation' (caru). Under the impact of the mantra placed by the guru on the disciple's hand, the hand moves spontaneously — the movement is called the 'hand of Śiva' (śivahasta) — and hits the body at a spot which indicates the kula to which the disciple belongs, for the body is a hierarchy of śaktis. This blow suddenly causes conviction (pratyaya).
The guru should light eight flawless lamps made of gold etc., with red wicks and ghee, worshipped according to the set of eight kula goddesses. Kuleśvara and Kuleśvarī are worshipped in the 'conch-shell' full of the nectar of bliss. By the 'hand of Śiva' the guru consecrates the disciple. Afterwards the Adept should undertake mantra practice.
The consecration of the Master: the qualified guru sets out sixty-four 'lamps' made with paste etc., worshipped according to the sixty-four kula goddesses; Kuleśvara and Kuleśvarī in the centre; he consecrates him as guru by the 'hand of Śiva'.
The yoginīs are usually sixty-four, interpreted as eight times the eight 'mothers' (mātṛkā); they belong to families (kula) or clans (gotra), with 8 major families (Brāhmī etc.) important at initiation, for the guru ascertains by the manner in which the flower falls to which family and kula the disciple belongs.
Jayaratha reports Abhinava esteemed the guru who follows the Kula ritual procedure (kulaprakriyā) more highly, because of its restfulness, than the guru devoted to tantra ritual procedure.
The role of 'Master': one who is an Adept and not consecrated as Master dispenses only supernatural powers; the Master who is a guru grants liberation as well. One may receive consecration (abhiṣeka) from a guru and so become a guru, albeit a 'formed' (kalpita) guru. There is therefore a hierarchy. The recipient of intense descent of energy does not need the external rite of purification, but the rite may be celebrated to manifest the real condition the akalpita guru has already received directly from the goddess.

[Kāmika Āgama]
First and most prestigious of the 28 principal Śaiva Tantras; authoritative for ritual in Tamil Nadu temples; Pūrvabhāga 75 chapters + Uttarabhāga 98 chapters, ~12,000 verses anuṣṭubh. Addresses temple ritual and personal worship, iconography. Śaiva Siddhānta canon, dualist.

[Sanskrit-trikashaivism, TĀ 23 translation excerpts]
TĀ 23.1-2: "Now the Supreme Lord's (pārameśvara) procedure (vidhiḥ) of consecration (abhiṣekasya) is declared (kathyate). This (eṣā) which is called initiation of the spiritual son (putraka-dīkṣā) is fit to join (yuktimat) a person to the categories that are objects of enjoyment..."
Kāmika citation: "He who does not know in this way the adhva-sandhāna (joining of the paths) is not at all a spiritual preceptor (daiśikaḥ) even if he has been consecrated through the succession starting with samayī."
Siddhayogīśvarīmata citation follows, same point.
TĀ 23.x (women/śūdra): "napuṃsakāḥ striyaḥ śūdrā ye cānye'pi tadarthinaḥ | te dīkṣāyāṃ na mīmāṃsyā jñānakāle vicārayet" — non-men, women, śūdras and others who desire it: they are not to be scrutinized at initiation; one should investigate at the time of knowledge.
TĀ 23.x: "Having worshipped and offered oblations like before, and having communicated the intention (cikīrṣitam), the guru should sprinkle (abhiṣiñcet) that disciple sixty-four times (catuḥṣaṣṭyā). Then once with the water full of the sap of those mantras (tad-mantra-rasa-toyena), according to the procedure stated before, with might and greatness (vibhavena), very extensively (suvistīrṇam)."
TĀ 23.x: "Thenceforth that former guru who has abandoned his authority (tyakta-adhikārakaḥ) acts as he wishes regarding explanation, initiation etc., without restriction. He is not bound, because a spiritual lineage (santānaḥ) is like a lamp kindled from a lamp (dīpa-dīpavat). There is no loss of authority, and he is not bound if he does not act. But if he does not perform it before dying, the uninterrupted transmission would be annihilated (vihanyeta)."
TĀ 23.x: "The guru is authorized regarding a group of four tasks (kārya-catuṣṭaye). There should be help for the fallen (patatām) in the form of lending a hand (hasta-ālambaḥ), and not the act of causing them to fall."
TĀ 23.x (sapta-satraka): "He should protect this group of seven sacrifices: (1) initiation (dīkṣā), (2) explanation (vyākhyā), (3) compassion (kṛpā), (4) friendship (maitrī) ... (7) the giving of food etc. (anna-ādi-dānam)."
TĀ 23.22-23: "During the procedure of consecration the collection of all instruments (sarva-upakaraṇa-vrātam), such as knife, chalk (karaṇī-khaṭikā-ādikam), is to be delivered by the guru to this learned disciple."
TĀ 23.102-103: "No assignment of adhikāra here, nor indeed the vow of knowledge (vidyā-vrata); what is to be conferred here is the sādhya-mantra in the course of the ritual. All instruction should be the delivery of one's own instruments; the procedure of consecration is declared as the Supreme Lord declared it."
TĀ 23 end colophon: iti kathitam...

[Dyczkowski, TĀ vol.9 ch.16-27 content note]
Volume nine contains chapters sixteen to twenty-seven. Begins with exposition of initiation into the condition of a teacher's apprentice (putraka) that can lead to consecration as teacher and priest (ācārya). Whereas the basic (samaya) initiation is performed with a single Trident maṇḍala, the power of this higher one is strongly reinforced by worship of three triads and incorporation of the worship of the Twelve Kālīs. Ch.23 is concerned with the consecration of a teacher and ch.24 with an initiate's funerary rites.

[TĀ structure context]

args.topic: Tantraloka 17 prameyaprakriya: procedures on the apprentice after initiation
args.excerpts:
[Dyczkowski vol.9 content note]
Chapter seventeen continues with a series of procedures concerning the apprentice: beginning with the fashioning of his sacred thread and the purification of the reality levels he is to traverse in the course of initiation. It continues with the inner illumination of his body with Mantra, the burning away of his fetters, his conjunction to the supreme principle and offerings to the fire.
[Ch.16] The rest of the initiation involves the complex projection (nyāsa) of layers of Mantras, beginning with those of the Six Paths, onto the neophant's body and the sacrificial area.

[sanskrit-trikashaivism TĀ 17 excerpts]
Chapter 17 = Prameyaprakriyā, 122 verses.
17.14: "Now I will speak the procedure (prakriyā) that gives identification with Bhairava (bhāvasyāhammayasvātmatādātmyāveśyamānatā)" — the procedure by which the state is unified with one's own self as 'I'.
Abhinavagupta will show how to manufacture Mantras for each tattva/category.
"yatra uddiṣṭe vidhau ... tad sādhyam anantaiḥ kriyātmakaiḥ aṃśaiḥ" — when a procedure has been stated, it is accomplished by endless ritual portions, as in the procedures of initiation; there should be no ūha (substitution/adaptation) there.
"pratāḍanam ... astreṇa ... tad-tattva-sthāne ... parimarśayet" — having struck the disciple with the weapon-Mantra (generally PHAṬ) at the place of that tattva, the guru should touch him.
"anye guravaḥ prāhuḥ īdṛśam bhāvanāmayam" — other gurus said such a procedure consists of contemplation (bhāvanāmaya), not physical ritual.
nibījā dīkṣā: if seedless initiation is to be performed, the guru throws another full oblation (pūrṇām āhuti) right there.
17.73: "eṣa hi śaktipātasya svabhāvaḥ, na pṛthak" — this is the essential nature of śaktipāta, not something separate.
[Tantrasara ch.17 correspondence] Liṅgoddhāra (removal of the mark) belongs to ch.22 in TĀ numbering; Tantrasāra's ch.17 covers the same initiatory arc compressed.

[TĀ structure]
Ch.15 ordinary initiation (samaya); 16 putraka initiation; 17 the procedures on the apprentice (thread, tattva purification, mantra illumination, fetter-burning, conjunction, fire offerings); 18 sūkṣmā dīkṣā (11v); 19 utkrānti (death) initiation; 20 tulā; 21 parokṣa (absent); 22 liṅgoddhāra (conversion); 23 abhiṣeka; 24 antyeṣṭi.

args.topic: Tantraloka 30 mantraugha: the multitude of Trika mantras
args.excerpts:
[sanskrit-trikashaivism TĀ 30 excerpts]
Chapter 30 = Mantraughaḥ / Mantrādi-prakāśana, 123 verses. "Now the suitable multitude of Mantras (yathocita-mantra-kadambaka) associated with the processes of the Trikakula (trikakula-krama-yogi) is described, for the sake of those whose minds have not yet ascended to vimarśa, so they may accomplish it gradually."
Monosyllabic mantras "residing in Kula (kula-sthāḥ)", "giving siddhis through the Kula-krama procedure (kula-krama-vidhānena) and by means of subtle knowledge (sūkṣma-vijñāna-yogataḥ)"; "to be followed always by a woman or by a man" — i.e. the Kula mantras are not restricted by sex.
Mantras "without aṅga, without family (aṅga-abhijana-varjitāḥ)" are to be worshipped by the best of adepts "according to the single-hero procedure (eka-vīra-vidhānataḥ)" — the deity without consort.
Lists: separate-seat worship (pṛthagāsana-pūjā) vs condensed worship (saṅkṣepa-pūjā) with mantra order; mantras ending in tālu (palate); Śrīmukuṭottara citations; Puruṣa/Prakṛti mantras; the twelve vowels (dvādaśa-svara) adorning bījas HRĪṂ KLĪṂ VLEṂ KLEṂ; "visarjayet tāḥ prathamam anyathā chidrayanti" — one should first discharge/dismiss them, otherwise they pierce (make holes).
[TĀ structure] Ch.28 parvan/calendar + circle sacrifice; 29 secret Kula ritual (rahasyacaryā); 30 mantra multitude of the Trikakula (mantraugha); 31 maṇḍala construction; 32 mudrās.

[Dupuche, Kula Ritual]
The supreme mantra of consciousness is SAUḤ, the supreme goddess Parā, expressing both the supreme reality and all that derives from it. The Kula ritual leads to mantra-vyāpti, the pervasion of the mantra; who knows this pervasion knows he is Bhairava. Chapter 29 is built on chapter 28. Six Kula sacrifices, each leading to a different aspect of the mantra. The practice is for "the most advanced gurus and disciples" (TĀ 29.2a).
